title: Comprehensive genomic characterization of radiation-related papillary thyroid cancer in the Ukraine
summary:
This cohort characterises papillary thyroid carcinoma arising in people who were children or in utero in Ukraine at the time of the 1986 Chernobyl accident, and it exists because no comparable exposure can ethically be reconstructed. Whole genome sequencing is available on 395 cases, RNA sequencing on 438 and microRNA on 437. The scientific question it was built for - what radiation does to a genome, and whether the resulting tumors differ mechanistically from sporadic ones - is answerable here and almost nowhere else.
It is also an object lesson in why a catalog entry is not enough. The harmonized clinical records report a median follow-up of 115 months - but that median rests on just 12 of the 449 cases. They also record vital status for 440 of 449 cases as "not reported". A researcher who selected this dataset on the strength of its follow-up figure would discover only after obtaining access that no survival analysis is possible, and that the follow-up figure itself rests on under 3% of the cohort.
one_liner: 449 papillary thyroid carcinomas from Ukrainians exposed to Chernobyl fallout as children - an irreplaceable radiation-exposure cohort with essentially no clinical annotation and no usable outcome data at all.

useful_for.question: What is the mutational and structural signature of ionising radiation exposure in a solid human tumor, and how does it scale with dose?
useful_for.rationale: Whole genome sequencing on 395 cases with structural variant and copy number calls on 394 supports genome-wide signature analysis, including the fusion-driven and small-deletion patterns the marker paper associated with radiation. This is the cohort's central strength and the reason it was assembled.
useful_for.statistical_note: Dose-response analysis requires the reconstructed individual dose estimates, which are not in the harmonized records. Without them this becomes an exposed-cohort description rather than a dose-response study.

useful_for.question: Do radiation-associated papillary thyroid carcinomas differ transcriptionally from sporadic ones, and can a classifier separate them?
useful_for.rationale: RNA sequencing on 438 cases and microRNA on 437 gives a well-powered expression cohort. TCGA-THCA provides a 507-case sporadic comparison group in the same repository with the same harmonization, which makes a cross-cohort contrast unusually tractable.
useful_for.statistical_note: Batch and platform differences between this cohort and TCGA-THCA are confounded with the exposure of interest. Any classifier must be evaluated with that confound stated, ideally with a batch-aware design rather than naive merging.

useful_for.question: Does age at exposure shape the resulting tumor genome, given that participants were children or in utero at the time?
useful_for.rationale: The cohort's defining feature is exposure during a developmental window. Age variables together with the genomic data allow the question to be posed, and it is one of the few human settings where exposure timing is externally fixed by a single dated event rather than self-reported.
useful_for.statistical_note: Age at diagnosis is not summarized in the harmonized records for this project, so age variables must be obtained through controlled access before this can be designed.

useful_for.question: Can microRNA profiles discriminate radiation-associated thyroid tumors, as a cheaper assay than whole genome sequencing for future screening cohorts?
useful_for.rationale: microRNA data exist on 437 of 449 cases, an unusually complete layer, and microRNA assays are far more tractable in resource-limited screening settings than sequencing.

limitations.statement: Vital status is populated for 98% of cases and informative for 0%: every populated value is "not reported". A follow-up time is derivable for just 12 of 449 cases, and even for those there is no outcome to pair it with, so no survival endpoint exists. No survival analysis of any kind is possible.
limitations.mitigation: None available within the dataset as distributed. Contact the submitting investigators through the dbGaP study page if outcome data are essential to your question, and do not plan the analysis on the assumption that they will be released.

limitations.statement: Race and ethnicity are recorded as "not reported" for all 440 cases with a value, and the cohort is drawn from one country and one exposure event. It describes Ukrainian patients exposed to a specific accident.
limitations.mitigation: Ancestry can be estimated from the germline sequence data if required, subject to the consent terms in the data use agreement.
